reasoning:
The test `themes_set_default_theme` fails at line 212 because `page.request.post('/themes/${originalDefault}/default')` in the `finally` block (line 209) does not actually restore the original default theme. The application has CSRF protection (security.py: `protect_unsafe_request`) that blocks all POST requests lacking an `X-CSRF-Token` header or `csrf_token` form field. The `page.request.post()` Playwright APIRequestContext call shares the session cookie but does not include the required CSRF token, so the server returns a 403 response. Playwright's APIRequestContext does not throw on non-2xx status codes, so the failure is silent — the default theme is never restored. The subsequent assertion at line 212 (`expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', originalDefault)`) then fails because the HTML element still carries `data-theme='spectestdefault-1785611850447'` (the test-created theme) instead of `'classic'` (the original default).

The same CSRF issue affects `deleteThemeViaApi` throughout the suite, but those calls all use `.catch(() => {})` which silently absorbs failures. The `themes_delete_custom_theme` test is skipped because the suite runs in serial mode and the preceding test (`themes_set_default_theme`) threw an unhandled error.

The CSRF bypass conditions (`TESTING` config, `DEMO_MODE` config) are not met — the Playwright tests connect to a standalone Flask app at port 5001, not through Flask's test client, so `app.config['TESTING']` is not set. Browser-based interactions (clicking buttons, submitting forms) work correctly because the page templates include the CSRF token in forms and htmx requests.
suggestedAction: Replace `page.request.post('/themes/${originalDefault}/default')` in the `finally` block of `themes_set_default_theme` with a browser-based interaction: navigate to `'/themes/${originalDefault}'` and click the 'Make default' button (which submits the form with a valid CSRF token). Also fix `deleteThemeViaApi` (used in all tests and `afterAll`) the same way — navigate to the theme page, click the delete button, and confirm the dialog — so that cleanup actually works instead of silently failing. This eliminates all raw `page.request.post()` calls that lack CSRF tokens.
